fills.reason: WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE are declared, and the collection (notes, media, review history) is written unencrypted to shared storage (legacy /sdcard/AnkiDroid) or app-specific external storage. Whether a user's flashcard collection counts as sensitive data is a product/privacy decision.

evidence.detail: Legacy collection directory sits on shared external storage.

fills.reason: Searched all non-test Kotlin/Java for SecretKeySpec, IvParameterSpec, Cipher.getInstance and KeyStore: none. The app does no app-level symmetric encryption, so it has no keys to hardcode.

Logging goes through Timber; the release tree drops VERBOSE/DEBUG. I searched for Timber calls that log password, hkey, token, username or email and found only a constant message about missing fields. No credentials are logged.
JavaScript is on in several WebViews (Info sets allowContentAccess=true), but setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs is never set to true anywhere, so the fail condition is not met.

allowFileAccess=true with JavaScript on in the reviewer, previewer and Info WebViews. However, neither allowFileAccessFromFileURLs nor allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs is set, and minSdk is 24 (≥16), so both default to false.
The only credential form (AnkiWeb login) uses inputType textPassword for the password and textNoSuggestions|textEmailAddress for the username, both non-caching.
The password field is an EditText with inputType textPassword (masked) and an optional password_toggle end icon. No Compose TextField is used for credentials.
FLAG_SECURE is not used anywhere. Screens show flashcard content and the AnkiWeb login (password masked). Whether a user's cards count as sensitive enough to block screenshots is a product decision.
Notifications show due-card counts, review-reminder titles, and sync progress/error messages. No PII, credentials or OTPs are put in setContentTitle/setContentText.

Two bridges exist: DeckOptions 'ankidroid' (onEvent only toggles modal open/close state) and PageFragment 'bridgeCommandInterface' (only runs a fixed map of UI commands such as unbury/customStudy). Pages load from the local AnkiServer, and DeckOptions only allows docs.ankiweb.net in-app. No exposed method handles sensitive data.

The app has a login screen (AnkiWeb credentials), and no overlay protection exists anywhere: no filterTouchesWhenObscured, onFilterTouchEventForSecurity, FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED checks or setHideOverlayWindows.

evidence.detail: The login button has no filterTouchesWhenObscured or other tapjacking protection.

fills.reason: SdCardReceiver tells the app's own activities about media eject/mount with implicit broadcasts (action only, no package or permission). Any app can register a receiver for com.ichi2.anki.action.MEDIA_EJECT/MOUNT and receive them.

evidence.detail: Implicit internal broadcast MEDIA_EJECT, no package set.
Implicit internal broadcast MEDIA_MOUNT, no package set.

fills.reason: The implicit internal broadcasts in SdCardReceiver carry no extras. The other implicit intents (ACTION_VIEW links, ACTION_OPEN/CREATE_DOCUMENT, TTS settings, MIUI settings) send user-selected or no extras to external handlers by design.

Every PendingIntent is immutable: PendingIntentCompat with isMutable=false, or FLAG_IMMUTABLE. Every base intent is explicit (Intent(context, X::class.java), DeferredNavigation destinations that resolve to explicit activity classes, or WorkManager's cancel intent).

IntentHandler declares a VIEW+BROWSABLE intent-filter with http/https data schemes (host="*", for .apkg/.colpkg/.csv/.tsv/.txt files) and no android:autoVerify. It is a generic file-handler filter that cannot be domain-verified, but it meets the test's fail condition.

evidence.detail: http deep link data element in an intent-filter without autoVerify.
https deep link data element in an intent-filter without autoVerify.

fills.reason: The only custom scheme (anki://x-callback-url/browser) reads the 'search' query parameter and passes it as free text to the Card Browser search UI. This is the accepted 'arbitrary search text' case; it is not used in a file path, raw SQL or WebView sink.

Read each exported activity. ManageSpaceActivity is the system manage-space entry. IntentHandler handles launch, file import (user confirms) and Tasker DO_SYNC (rate-limited sync of the user's own account). The PROCESS_TEXT aliases and IntentHandler2/InstantNoteEditor open note/browser UI with shared text. Reviewer opens the study UI. None returns data to the caller or bypasses an authentication step.

AnkiDroidWidgetSmall and AddNoteWidget are AppWidgetProviders that only refresh RemoteViews. SdCardReceiver acts only on ACTION_MEDIA_EJECT/MOUNTED, which are protected system broadcasts that third-party apps cannot send.
java.util.Random / kotlin.random are used only to name a downloaded file and pick an index in NoteFieldDecorator. Neither is a security-relevant value; no tokens, keys or passwords are generated.
System.currentTimeMillis/Calendar are used for timing and scheduling (elapsed time, day cutoff), not to generate tokens, keys or passwords.
No KeyGenerator or KeyPairGenerator in any non-test source; the app generates no cryptographic keys.
No Cipher.getInstance, SecretKeyFactory or KeyGenerator in any non-test source; the app does no symmetric encryption.
No Cipher.getInstance in any non-test source; no block cipher modes are used.
No KeyGenParameterSpec or KeyPairGenerator in any non-test source; no asymmetric key pairs.
The only JCA getInstance calls are MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA1") with no explicit provider.

No KeyguardManager.isDeviceSecure/isKeyguardSecure or BiometricManager.canAuthenticate anywhere in the code. The app has no local authentication and no Keystore-protected secrets, so whether a screen-lock check is wanted is a product decision.
No BiometricPrompt, BiometricManager or setAllowedAuthenticators in any source; the app has no biometric authentication.
No BiometricPrompt usage in any source; the app has no biometric authentication.
No KeyGenParameterSpec / setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment in any source.
No BiometricPrompt / setConfirmationRequired in any source.
No KeyGenParameterSpec / setUserAuthenticationParameters in any source.

The only Kotlin HTTP client (OkHttp in HttpFetcher) uses default connection specs. Nothing calls SSLContext.getInstance with an old TLS version, setEnabledProtocols, ConnectionSpec or tlsVersions. AnkiWeb sync runs in the native Rust backend, which this check doesn't cover.

The only hardcoded http:// URL used for traffic is the in-process loopback AnkiServer (http://127.0.0.1:port) serving local pages to WebViews. Other http:// strings are XML namespaces, a doc comment and a browser-resolution probe intent. No remote endpoint is contacted over http.
No SSLSocket in any Java/Kotlin source; networking uses OkHttp, which verifies hostnames.
No custom X509TrustManager or checkServerTrusted in any Java/Kotlin source.
No custom HostnameVerifier in any Java/Kotlin source; the OkHttp builder keeps the default verifier.
No WebViewClient overrides onReceivedSslError, so WebView's default (cancel) applies. Checked the clients in the reviewer, previewer, Info, SharedDecks, RemoveAccount and the Page fragments.

ProviderInstaller.installIfNeeded is not called anywhere. The app also ships non-GMS builds (Amazon, F-Droid), where the GMS provider is unavailable, so whether to add it to the Play build is a product decision.

The network security config has no pin-set. I also found no code pinning (no CertificatePinner or custom TrustManager in Kotlin/Java). The app may need to stay unpinned because it supports custom sync servers, but the pinning condition is not met.

evidence.detail: base-config with no pin-set or domain-config pinning.

fills.reason: WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled is called at startup with a user preference, not gated on FLAG_DEBUGGABLE. The developer-options switch that sets it is shown only in non-debug (release) builds, so release users can turn on WebView remote debugging.

evidence.detail: WebView debugging is turned on from a preference, without checking FLAG_DEBUGGABLE.
The JavaScript-debugging switch is visible in release builds.

fills.reason: RemoveAccountFragment's shouldOverrideUrlLoading returns false (load in-app) for every URL that isn't a redirect target, so this JavaScript-enabled WebView will follow links to any domain. The other WebViews do restrict navigation: SharedDecks uses a host allowlist, DeckOptions allows docs.ankiweb.net, Info only the changelog, and the reviewer sends external links out.

evidence.detail: Any URL that isn't a redirect target is loaded in-app; there is no host allowlist.

fills.reason: The manifest has no android.webkit.WebView.EnableSafeBrowsing=false meta-data and the code never calls setSafeBrowsingEnabled(false).
The native libraries (Anki Rust backend) come in a prebuilt dependency, not built from this source; checking PIC needs the built APK's .so files.
The native libraries come in a prebuilt dependency (Rust backend); checking stack canaries needs the built APK's .so files.
The app checks the OS version with Build.VERSION.SDK_INT in many places (e.g. AnkiActivity, DeckPicker, InitialActivity).
Needs an SBOM of the resolved (including transitive) dependencies uploaded to Dependency-Track; Ward's MASTG-TEST-0272 covers direct dependencies only.

getSerializable/getSerializableExtra read the app's own saved-instance state and fragment arguments, plus MultimediaActivity extras (not exported). All are typed through CompatHelper (class-checked on API 33+). There is no ObjectInputStream on external data.
No security decision is made from locally stored data: there are no entitlement/premium flags or trial counters. The stored AnkiWeb host key is a credential the server validates.

In CardContentProvider.query, the NOTES_V2 route puts the caller-supplied selection string (and sort order) straight into the WHERE/ORDER BY clause of a raw SQL query. A client app with the provider permission can inject SQL against the whole collection database.

evidence.detail: Caller-controlled selection and order are put into the SQL string.
evidence.quote: SQLiteQueryBuilder.buildQueryString(false, "notes", proj, selection, null, null, order, null)

fills.reason: No forced-update mechanism (no Play In-App Updates, no backend minimum-version gate). The app is distributed outside Play too, so whether to force updates is a product decision.
build.gradle reads targetSdk from the version catalog, which sets targetSdk = "36". That meets the API 36 requirement.
The release build type doesn't set debuggable (only debug sets it true; benchmark sets false). The manifest has no android:debuggable, and the buildSrc convention plugins don't set it.
The release signing config doesn't disable v2/v3 signing or force v1-only, so AGP defaults (v2+ for minSdk 24) apply.
The release key comes from the KEYSTOREPATH env var (or a fallback keystore in tools/); the key size can only be read from the signed APK or the keystore.
No StrictMode API calls in app sources; the only match is a KDoc reference in ResolveInfoCompat.
The native libraries come in a prebuilt dependency; checking for debug symbols needs the built APK's .so files.
No root-detection code found (no RootBeer, su-path, test-keys or similar checks). The app protects no high-value assets, so whether root detection is wanted is a product decision.
No debugger detection found (no Debug.isDebuggerConnected or TracerPid checks). Whether it is wanted for this app is a product decision.
R8 minification is on for release (proguard-android-optimize). Judging how well security-relevant logic is obfuscated needs the decompiled release APK.
The native code comes in a prebuilt dependency; judging its obfuscation needs the built .so files.

The app sends app-activity data (screen views, events, exceptions) with a persistent client ID to Google Analytics through the com.criticalay GoogleAnalytics SDK. Sending is opt-in, but the data must be declared.
